head.h1: Iftar Catering in Dubai — Real Prices, Menus and Timings

opening_paragraph: Iftar catering in Dubai from myCHEF starts at AED 150 per person for a full buffet and AED 700 for a plated private chef. The figure is quoted to your guest count, menu and service level. A vetted private chef plans the meal, cooks on site, serves and clears up, so you break the fast with your guests instead of with the kitchen. Share the date, the numbers and the venue, we typically reply within 15 minutes during business hours, with an itemised proposal to follow you can read at a glance.

replace_in_block.new_heading: What iftar catering in Dubai includes
new_paragraphs: Full iftar catering services in Dubai cover the whole sunset meal end to end — menu design, cooking on site, service staff, plating, setup and cleanup — for one per-person price. When you hire iftar catering in Dubai through myCHEF, a single team owns the evening: the chef builds a menu around your taste and guest count, arrives with the ingredients and equipment, times the food to Maghrib, and leaves the kitchen as they found it. Because we work as a private iftar chef service instead of a fixed-menu factory, every booking is bespoke. That matters during Ramadan, when guests arrive hungry after a long fast and the first plate — dates, laban, a warming soup — needs to land the moment the call to prayer sounds. Whether it is an intimate family majlis or a large iftar catering company brief for hundreds, the format flexes to the room while the standard stays the same.

MyCHEF was founded by a chef trained in some of Europe's most demanding kitchens, on one idea: you own the evening, we carry the work. Chefs and partner kitchens reach iftar catering through myCHEF's 12-stage partner verification framework — licensing, food-safety documentation, capability, experience and reference checks — which we are currently implementing across the partner base. We are honest about it, too: no system removes every risk, so we match each event to the best available chef for it.

For an iftar, that is usually Layla Hassan — 14+ years in Lebanese and Emirati kitchens running catering for prestige events. Her mezze, charcoal grills and aromatic rice are built for sharing, and she is especially sought after for Ramadan and Eid, which makes her a natural fit as your private iftar chef. Alongside iftar catering we have delivered villa weddings, yacht celebrations and corporate galas in Dubai. Real client reviews for Iftar catering are published as events happen.

replace_in_block.new_heading: How much does iftar catering cost in Dubai?
new_paragraphs: Iftar catering in Dubai starts from AED 150 per person for a full buffet, and the final iftar catering price depends on guest count, menu and service level. A drop-off spread is the most affordable iftar catering per head, from AED 90; the AED 150 tier covers a premium buffet with live stations and extended mezze; a plated dinner cooked and served course by course by a private chef runs AED 700 to AED 950. Buffet service starts at 20 guests, every other format at 10, and the minimum order is AED 900. Larger guest counts usually lower the per-person cost. Curated catering packages bundle menu, staff and setup at set price points, which many hosts find easier than pricing each line. For a full breakdown of iftar catering cost in Dubai and what drives it, see our Dubai catering price guide , or send your numbers for an itemised quote — no guessing, no hidden extras.

add_block.new_heading: The full iftar menu, course by course
new_paragraphs: If you are working out what to eat for iftar and want more than a category list, this is the menu our chefs build from, set out in serving order. A set menu is normally written as a choice from each section — at the entry tier five cold mezze, three hot mezze, three grills, three mains and three desserts; at the premium tier eight, five, five, four and five. A full buffet runs wider than that and adds live stations. Buffet service starts at 20 guests, every other format at 10, and the minimum order value is AED 900.
At Maghrib — the fast-breaking course
This is its own course, staged away from the buffet and standing ready before the call to prayer. Getting it right is most of the evening.
Medjool dates, a three-premium-date selection, dried apricots, figs, almonds and pistachios.
Fresh fruit cuts and an exotic fresh fruit platter.
Gahwa poured from the dallah, karak tea, laban.
Jallab, Qamar al-Din, Vimto, Rooh Afza, passion fruit sarbat, watermelon mint cooler, fresh watermelon juice, mint lemonade.
Thari Kanji — the Kerala rice-and-vermicelli porridge many Malayali households break the fast on, in place of dates.
Soups
One or two on a set menu, three or four on a large buffet. Lentil is close to compulsory.
Lentil soup · Harira · Chicken soup · Mushroom soup · Seafood soup · Chicken tom yam goong.
Cold mezze and salads
Pick five, six or eight depending on the tier. The full list is published here so you can see exactly what a tier upgrade buys instead of guessing.

From the charcoal

Main courses — Levantine, Gulf and Emirati

Three or four on a set menu, five to eight across a full buffet. The Emirati dishes are the ones guests notice, and they are cooked by chefs who cook them for a living, not by a Levantine chef improvising.
Lamb ouzi — whole or half lamb on a rice platter, or ouzi stuffed with warak enab, carved in front of guests.
Lamb saddle · Stuffed lamb · Stuffed chicken · Chicken roast with rice platter · Slow-braised lamb shoulder with pilaf and roasted almonds.
Chicken kabsah · Lamb kabseh · Mandi · Madfoon · Haneeth · Mathbi · Seafood machboos · Fish sayadieh.
Harees · Veal harees · Thareed · Madrouba · Saloona · Balaleet — the Emirati heritage line.
Jordanian mansaf · Chicken moghrabieh · Chicken mousakhan · Chicken freekeh · Lamb makloubeh with eggplant · Shawarma fatteh with tahini sauce · Chicken fatteh.
Dawood basha · Kebbe bil laban · Shakrieh · Fasoulia stew · Green pea stew · Mloukhieh — each served with rice.
Lamb tagine · Butternut squash tagine · Algerian couscous casserole · Moroccan-style braised beef brisket · Lemon chicken with zaatar yogurt · Seafood paella.
Main courses — South Asian
Not a sub-section but a parallel track. Plenty of Dubai iftars run South Asian end to end, and the naming matters: Thalassery biryani is not the same dish as a generic one.
Thalassery chicken biryani · Thalassery mutton biryani · Chicken biryani · Meat biryani · Vegetable biryani · Chicken pulao.

Rice, sides and breads
Oriental rice · Ghee rice · Arabic rice · Stuffed zucchini · Vegetable stew.
Assorted Arabic bread · Saj bread · Rigag · Khameer · Naan · Paratha · Coin paratha · Nice pathiri · Ney pathal · Assorted rotis.

Live stations

Stations are quoted as discrete units, not folded into the per-head buffet price, and the chef and the setup are part of the station price. Each one is written into your proposal with the capacity it is being built for, so you know what it covers before the night. One to three stations suit a mid-sized buffet; villa, majlis and Ramadan-tent events usually run more.
Full roasted lamb station with a carver, and an ouzi carving station.
Barbecue station — shish tawouk, grilled meat, kafta, arayess kafta, lamb chops.
Shawarma station — chicken, beef or Mexican, off a vertical spit.
Saj station — zaatar, cheese, meat, turkey and cheese, Nutella, baked live on the dome.
Manakish station and a falafel station fried to order.
Cheese kunafa station and a live luqaimat station , the two desserts worth watching.
Pasta station — bolognese, alfredo, arabiata, four cheese · burger station · fajita station
Gahwa and Turkish coffee station · fresh juice station

Which of those stations can run is decided by the address. The saj travels widest: an electric dome needs no fuel approval and works in a villa kitchen, on a terrace, or inside an apartment on a socket with headroom, while a gas saj stays outdoors at ground level at a villa, because the UAE Fire Code keeps LPG cylinders out of indoor spaces (11-2.2.6) and off roofs and terraces (Table 11.1). On a yacht neither the saj nor the shawarma spit comes aboard: D-Marin Art. 53.1(a) allows only the vessel's own installed gas supply, and Dubai Harbour section 7.4 prohibits operating gas cylinders on marina premises. An iftar on the water therefore runs the carving stations, a cold mezze bar and induction, with the breads baked in the licensed kitchen and the shawarma cone cooked on its skewer ashore and carved live on deck — guests get the same shaved-to-order ritual, and the fire happened two hours earlier. Charter crews run the boat's own fitted grill themselves, so the chef preps, plates and serves alongside it. For a rooftop or a desert camp, myCHEF confirms the setup with the building management or the site before quoting.

new_paragraphs: The single thing that makes or breaks an iftar is timing to Maghrib, and that is where a professional team earns its place. Our chef and service staff arrive early, set the buffet or tables, and have the fast-breaking course — dates, water, laban, soup — ready to serve the instant the fast opens, then keep the mains flowing as guests return from prayer. We coordinate prayer timing, plan the buffet layout so the lines do not tangle, and manage the kitchen so nothing runs out at the worst moment. For larger events we bring enough staff to plate, replenish and clear without a fuss, and we build a prayer break into the running order. This is the difference between drop-off trays and true iftar catering services in Dubai: someone is watching the clock and the room so you do not have to.

Maghrib is the trigger, and it moves. Sunset in Dubai shifts by roughly a minute a day, so the serve time on the first night of Ramadan is not the serve time on the last, and we work to the published prayer timetable for your specific date instead of to a fixed hour. The running order we plan to is simple. The fast-breaking course — dates, water, laban, soup — stands ready 20 minutes before the adhan and is served the moment it sounds. The mains open 20 to 25 minutes after that, once guests are back from Maghrib prayer. Dessert, gahwa and karak run long, because that is the part of the evening nobody wants hurried. Tell us when you book whether the group prays together on site, because it changes when the buffet opens.

add_block.new_heading: Hosting iftar at home compared with a hotel iftar buffet
new_paragraphs: Most people searching for iftar in Dubai are choosing between two different purchases: a seat at a hotel or restaurant iftar buffet, and hosting at home. A buffet seat is priced per person, you travel to it, you eat inside a set sitting of about two hours, and the room is shared with everyone else who booked that night. Catering at home is also priced per person — from AED 150 for a full buffet — but the chef comes to you, the majlis stays yours for as long as the evening runs, and the menu is written for your family instead of for two hundred strangers.

Which one wins turns on headcount. For two or four people a hotel sitting is usually the simpler choice, and we will tell you so. From around ten or twelve guests upward a home iftar starts to make sense on both cost and comfort: no per-seat premium for the venue, elderly relatives and small children in a familiar room, prayer on your own timetable instead of between sittings, and the leftovers stay with you. Buffet service at home starts at 20 guests, every other format at 10, and the minimum order is AED 900. If you would rather the chef cooked and plated course by course than set out a buffet, that is a private-chef dinner at AED 700 to AED 950 per person.

add_block.new_heading: How to hire iftar catering in Dubai
new_paragraphs: Hiring iftar catering in Dubai takes three steps. First, tell us the date, the guest count and the venue — an office, a villa, a majlis — and roughly the style you want. We typically reply within 15 minutes during business hours with a menu direction and an itemised quote. Second, we refine the menu together, lock the dietary requirements and confirm the staffing and timing to Maghrib; this is also when we match your named chef. Third, on the day the team arrives early, sets up, serves and cleans up, and you enjoy the evening. Because Ramadan dates fill fast, a week is usually enough notice for a small gathering, but book earlier for large parties, corporate iftars and peak nights. Looking for iftar catering near me anywhere across the city? We cover all of Dubai.

add_block.new_heading: Planning iftar catering step by step
new_paragraphs: Send your date, guest count and venue — your iftar catering proposal arrives.
Book as early as you can — the whole city wants the same evening, and the date is set by the calendar, not by you.
Confirm what goes on the iftar catering menu 7 days out, once the count settles.
Ask for special diets up front; iftar catering plates are planned, not improvised inside 48 hours .
Check loading and access details; allow 2 hours of iftar catering setup on site.
Plan on roughly 3 hours of iftar catering service, and add 5% VAT to the total.

As guidance and not a promise, standard private-chef experiences suit about 48 hours' notice, standard catering packages 72 hours, live cooking stations and multi-staff events three to five days, bespoke menus and larger private events five to seven days, and weddings, corporate functions and complex productions seven to fourteen days or more.

We recommend booking as early as possible. Lead times depend on guest numbers, menu complexity, staffing, equipment, location and partner availability. Booking late for a iftar? Send the date first; whether it works depends on which partners are free.

new_paragraphs: An iftar menu in Dubai traditionally opens the fast gently and then builds to a full spread — and ours does the same, tailored to your guests. We start with dates, laban and soups (lentil or harees), move into a mezze table of hummus, moutabbel, fattoush, sambousek and kibbeh, then a main buffet of charcoal grills, machboos or ouzi, aromatic rice and slow-cooked stews, closing with Arabic sweets, kunafa and fresh fruit. An Arabic and international buffet is the most requested iftar food catering in Dubai format, but partners also plate, run live stations or build a lighter healthy spread. Every dish is halal, and dietary needs — vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free — are handled without a separate, sad "special" tray. Treat these as starting points: your final iftar menu is written with you.
